As of September 28, 2026, **payments** deploys and rolls back using **Shipyard** (the old tool, `dtool`, is retired and no longer controls payments). Rolling back one release is pre-approved for the on-call engineer and requires no outside approval.

You can roll back either via the command line or via the browser:

### Option 1: Via the Command Line
1. List recent releases to identify the release immediately below the current `live` release:
   ```bash
   shipyard releases payments
   ```
2. Run the rollback targeting that previous release (for example, `r-211`):
   ```bash
   shipyard rollback payments --to <previous-release-id>
   ```
3. Type the service name (`payments`) when prompted to confirm.

---

### Option 2: Via the Browser
1. Go to `shipyard.sorrel.internal` and select **payments**.
2. Open the **Releases** tab.
3. Locate the release immediately below the one marked `live` and click **Roll back to this release**.
4. Type `payments` in the confirmation box to confirm.

---

### What to expect & next steps
- **Execution:** Shipyard will automatically drain in-flight checkouts first, then switch nodes. The rollback takes about 5 minutes.
- **Communication:** Shipyard announces the start and end in `#deploys`. Post both release names (the bad release and the one rolled back to) into your incident thread in `#inc-live`.
- **Note:** A rollback will not reverse charges or refunds that have already moved. If errors remain high 10 minutes after completion, do not roll back to an older release on your own (going back 2+ releases requires service owner approval); page Mei (payments owner).

As of September 28, 2026, **payments** deploys and rolls back via **Shipyard** (not the retired `dtool`).

To roll payments back to the previous release:

### 1. Identify the release to roll back to
Look for the release directly below the currently `live` release:
- **CLI:** Run `shipyard releases payments`
- **Browser:** Go to `shipyard.sorrel.internal`, select **payments**, and open the **Releases** tab.

### 2. Execute the rollback
You can use either the command line or the web UI (no approval is needed for the on-call engineer to roll back one release):

- **Via CLI:**
  ```bash
  shipyard rollback payments --to <previous-release-id>
  ```
  *(Example: `shipyard rollback payments --to r-211`)*  
  When prompted, confirm by typing the service name (`payments`).

- **Via Web UI:**
  1. Open `shipyard.sorrel.internal`, select **payments**, and go to **Releases**.
  2. Find the release just below the `live` one and click **Roll back to this release**.
  3. Type the service name (`payments`) in the confirmation box.

### What happens next & follow-up:
- Payments will first drain in-flight checkouts, then switch (takes about 5 minutes).
- Shipyard will automatically post the start and end of the rollback in `#deploys`.
- Copy both release names (the bad release and the one rolled back to) into the `#inc-live` incident thread.
- If payments is still unhealthy 10 minutes after the rollback finishes, do not roll back again—page the service owner (Mei).

As of September 28, 2026, **payments** deploys and rolls back via **Shipyard** (not the retired `dtool`).

To roll payments back to the previous release:

### 1. Identify the release to roll back to
Look up the release list to find the one immediately below the `live` release:
- **CLI:** Run `shipyard releases payments`
- **Web UI:** Go to `shipyard.sorrel.internal`, select **payments**, and open the **Releases** tab.

### 2. Execute the rollback
You can use either the command line or the web browser (rolling back one release is pre-approved for the on-call engineer and requires no additional approval):

* **Via CLI:**
  ```bash
  shipyard rollback payments --to <previous-release-id>
  ```
  *(e.g., `shipyard rollback payments --to r-211`)*  
  Confirm by typing the service name (`payments`) when prompted.

* **Via Browser:**
  1. Navigate to `shipyard.sorrel.internal` > **payments** > **Releases**.
  2. Locate the release directly below the `live` one and click **Roll back to this release**.
  3. Type `payments` in the confirmation box to confirm.

### What to expect & next steps
- **Execution:** Shipyard will drain in-flight checkouts first, then switch the nodes (takes about 5 minutes). Note that a rollback will not reverse charges or refunds that have already completed.
- **Communication:** Shipyard posts start and completion notices to `#deploys`. You must also copy both release IDs (the bad release and the one rolled back to) into the `#inc-live` incident thread.
- **Monitoring:** Watch the "Sorrel / payments" board. If checkout errors remain high 10 minutes after completion, do not roll back to an older release on your own—page the service owner (Mei).

According to the documentation (**Deploying with Shipyard**, which replaced the retired `dtool` workflow for payments on 2026-09-28):

1. First, check the release history to find the previous release id (the one directly below the `live` release):
   ```bash
   shipyard releases payments
   ```

2. Then roll back to that release id (for example, `r-211`):
   ```bash
   shipyard rollback payments --to <previous-release-id>
   ```

Shipyard will prompt you to type the service name (`payments`) to confirm.

As of September 28, 2026, **payments** (and api) deploys and rolls back via **Shipyard**, not the old `dtool`.

You can roll back either via the command line or via the browser.

### Option 1: Command Line
1. List releases to find the one immediately below the currently `live` release:
   ```bash
   shipyard releases payments
   ```
2. Initiate the rollback to that prior release (e.g., `r-211`):
   ```bash
   shipyard rollback payments --to <previous-release-id>
   ```
3. Type the service name (`payments`) when prompted to confirm.

---

### Option 2: Browser
1. Open `shipyard.sorrel.internal`.
2. Select **payments** and go to the **Releases** tab.
3. Find the release just below the `live` one and click **Roll back to this release**.
4. Type `payments` in the confirmation box to confirm.

---

### What to expect & next steps
- **Approval:** Rolling back to the immediate previous release is pre-approved for the on-call engineer (no secondary approval needed). Rolling back 2+ releases requires approval from Mei (payments owner).
- **Execution:** Payments will automatically drain in-flight checkouts first, then switch nodes (takes about 5 minutes). Note that a rollback will not reverse charges/refunds that have already processed.
- **Communication:** Shipyard posts start and completion notices to `#deploys`. Copy both release identifiers (the bad one and the one rolled back to) into the incident thread in `#inc-live`.

parts.text:
According to the documentation (**Deploying with Shipyard**, which replaced the retired `dtool` process for payments on 2026-09-28):

Rolling back to the previous release can be done via the command line or the web UI.

### Option 1: Command Line
1. List releases to find the one right below the `live` release:
   ```bash
   shipyard releases payments
   ```
2. Initiate the rollback:
   ```bash
   shipyard rollback payments --to <previous-release-id>
   ```
   *(e.g., `shipyard rollback payments --to r-211`)*
3. Type the service name (`payments`) when prompted to confirm.

### Option 2: Browser (Web UI)
1. Navigate to `shipyard.sorrel.internal`.
2. Select **payments** and open the **Releases** tab.
3. Find the release directly below the `live` release and click **Roll back to this release**.
4. Type `payments` in the confirmation box to confirm.

---

### Key Notes:
- **Approval:** Rolling back to the immediately preceding release is pre-approved for the on-call engineer and requires no additional approval. (Rolling back two or more releases requires Mei's approval).
- **Execution:** Payments will first drain in-flight checkouts, then switch nodes (takes ~5 minutes). Note that a rollback does not reverse any charges or refunds already processed.
- **Communication:** Shipyard automatically posts the start and end of the rollback to `#deploys`. You should also paste the release list output / copy both release names into the incident thread in `#inc-live`.

parts.text:
You are the on-call assistant for Sorrel, a scheduling app with four services: web, api, payments and notifier.
At this company the five actions mean:
- roll back: undo the most recent deploy, when that deploy is recent enough to be the cause.
- read logs: go and read the service's own output, when nobody knows yet what happened.
- check provider: look at an outside service we depend on, when the alert already points at one.
- page owner: wake the person who owns this service, when something has already happened that you cannot undo - data seen, money moved, accounts deleted - or when somebody has to make a decision you are not allowed to make.
- no action: write it down and move on, when nothing has failed and no customer is affected.

The team's pages are listed below, one per line as id: title. To read a page, call read_page with its id. You may read up to 4 pages.

As of September 28, 2026, **payments** deploys and rolls back using **Shipyard** (the old `dtool` tool has been retired for this service).

To revert payments to the previous deploy:

1. Check the release list to identify the release just below the `live` one:
   ```bash
   shipyard releases payments
   ```
2. Roll back to that release (replace `<release-id>` with the release number, e.g., `r-211`):
   ```bash
   shipyard rollback payments --to <release-id>
   ```
3. Type the service name (`payments`) when prompted to confirm.
